headline: Lithuania Orders Shelters After Unidentified Object Alert
deck: Lithuania issued a red alert and shelter order after detecting an unidentified object; NATO fighters were scrambled and Kaunas airport closed.

evidence_box.fragment: Lithuanian authorities issued a red air warning and ordered residents in central and northern parts of the country to go to shelters after detecting an unrecognized flying object.
evidence_box.source: Straits Times / Reuters report, captured by research sensor

source_note.raw_excerpt: On the morning of 18 October 2026, Lithuanian authorities issued a red air warning and ordered residents in central and northern parts of the country to go to shelters for about an hour due to an unrecognized flying object.

evidence_box.fragment: Officials described the object as most likely a drone, but its identity and origin were unresolved.
evidence_box.source: Straits Times / Reuters report, captured by research sensor

source_note.raw_excerpt: The object was described by officials as most likely a drone. Exact identity and origin of the object, including whether it was a drone, remained unresolved.

evidence_box.fragment: The warning covered areas including Šiauliai and Panevėžys.
evidence_box.source: Straits Times / Reuters report, captured by research sensor

source_note.raw_excerpt: The red warning covered central and northern parts of Lithuania, including the Šiauliai and Panevėžys areas.

evidence_box.fragment: NATO air-policing fighters were scrambled and Kaunas airport was temporarily closed.
evidence_box.source: Straits Times / Reuters report, captured by research sensor

source_note.raw_excerpt: Authorities scrambled NATO air-policing fighters and temporarily closed Kaunas airport.

evidence_box.fragment: Latvian forces briefly issued and then dropped a yellow warning in border regions.
evidence_box.source: Straits Times / Reuters report, captured by research sensor

source_note.raw_excerpt: Latvian forces briefly issued then dropped a yellow warning in border regions.

evidence_box.fragment: After the object disappeared, its identity or origin had not been confirmed.
evidence_box.source: Straits Times / Reuters report, captured by research sensor

source_note.raw_excerpt: After the object disappeared, officials had not confirmed its identity or origin.

evidence_box.fragment: Vilmantas Vitkauskas, head of Lithuania's National Crisis Management Centre, said the latest information indicated an airborne threat that was most likely a drone.

source_note.raw_excerpt: – De siste opplysningene tyder på at det er identifisert en trussel fra luften, og at det mest sannsynlig dreier seg om en drone, sier lederen for Litauens nasjonale krisehåndteringssenter (NKVC) Vilmantas Vitkauskas til den litauiske radiokanalen LRT.
source_note.provenance_note: Verbatim text captured by the research sensor from the source page.

body: Lithuanian authorities issued a red air warning and ordered residents in central and northern parts of the country to go to shelters for about an hour after detecting an unrecognized flying object. [E1]
The warning covered central and northern Lithuania, including the Šiauliai and Panevėžys areas. [E3]
Officials described the object as most likely a drone, while its exact identity and origin remained unresolved. [E2]
Vilmantas Vitkauskas, head of Lithuania’s National Crisis Management Centre, told Lithuanian radio station LRT that the latest information indicated an airborne threat most likely to be a drone. [E7]
Latvian forces briefly issued a yellow warning in border regions and then withdrew it. [E5]
After the object disappeared, Lithuanian officials had not confirmed its identity or origin. [E6]
